evidence.note: First full suite surfaced 10 failures; agent diagnosed each to a distinct real cause (tuple flattening, #N/A classification, error-inspecting predicates, LET-lambda dispatch, WebSocket support, iterative-calc stop) instead of symptom-patching — root-cause fixing per feature (anchor 5).

Recognized WebSocket failure as a missing upgrade/library capability, fixed the dependency in start.sh, restarted, and re-verified the previously-failing subset before a full rerun — targeted diagnosis + re-verification.

Own custom check (not in smoke suite) revealed openpyxl(data_only=True) couldn't read cached values. Agent iterated through two separate root causes — absolute /xl/ rel targets + empty <v/>, then relationship attribute ordering — re-checking after each restart until it passed. Reworking the OOXML approach when openpyxl couldn't read the export (anchor 8 example).
Preemptively raised recursion ceiling so long formula chains don't fail topo traversal — smaller adaptation to anticipated hidden-suite stress.

reasoning: Across the whole arc the agent reliably diagnosed and fixed the true cause of each failing feature and re-verified (anchor 5), and in the XLSX/openpyxl episode it treated a surprising read failure as a signal about its OOXML export approach, iterating through two distinct root causes with restart-and-recheck loops until the export became openpyxl-readable — the anchor-8 example. It stops short of 8+ because corrections were within-approach patches rather than a decisive re-architecture and no foundational assumption was overturned early, placing it at a solid 7 between anchors 5 and 8.
